items: Questions frequently test classification: differentiate between Constitutional Bodies (e.g., CAG, UPSC, Election Commission), Statutory Bodies (e.g., NHRC, SEBI), and Executive Bodies (e.g., NITI Aayog).
Note the key constitutional articles: Article 148 (CAG), Article 280 (Finance Commission), Article 315 (UPSC), and Article 324 (Election Commission).
Remember that non-constitutional bodies can be established by ordinary law (Statutory) or executive notification (Non-statutory/Executive).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional bodies derive their powers, duties, and structure directly from the text of the Constitution of India.
According constitutional status to a body or institution ensures independence, financial autonomy, and protection from arbitrary executive interference.
The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992 conferred constitutional status on Panchayati Raj Institutions and Municipalities respectively.
Any modification to the powers or composition of constitutional bodies generally requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
